newsitem.title: UK: BBC drops black comedy after food poison outbreak.
newsitem.headline: BBC drops black comedy after food poison outbreak.

text.p: The BBC has decided not to show a television black comedy about "mad turkey disease" because of a food poisoning outbreak in Scotland which has killed 12 people.

"Gobble" was due to be screened next Saturday but British Broadcasting Corporation executives decided it would be inappropriate because of the food poisoning which has made more than 300 people ill. The outbreak has been linked to products from two butcher's shops.
"The BBC has decided that it is not appropriate at this particular time. It is mainly the fact that it was such a tragic outbreak," a BBC spokesman said.
"Gobble" is about a food scare that starts when a mistaken link is made between turkeys and a fatal illness in humans.
The film was originally intended as a satire on how the government has handled previous food scares like so-called mad cow disease.
